To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HLA class I (A, B, C) and class II (DRB1, DQB1) diversity in Mexican admixture individuals from the central region of Mexico is primarily from Amerindians and Caucasians with small contributions of Africans and recent Asians.

we identified HLA blocks and conserved haplotypes of Amerindian, African, Caucasian and Asian origin in Mexicans from the Central area of Mexico, which will help to improve the knowledge about the HLA diversity of this population and to better understand the genetic background of Mexicans.

we found a great diversity of MHC blocks and conserved haplotypes in Mexican admixed population and the ancestral contribution to these blocks and haplotypes was mainly from Amerindian origin with a smaller contribution of Caucasian origin, and also we found a correlation between HLA-B and STR markers that could be used to infer the ancestry of MHC blocks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the diversity of HLA class 1 and class II alleles in Mexicans and their contribution to the understanding of human diversity in admixed populations.
the genetic diversity of the HLA class I, class II, and the STRs in the MHC in Mexican individuals and their implications for the study of genetic diversity in admixed populations.
the study of the MHC class I and class II diversity and their conserved haplotypes and blocks, and their contribution to the study of population genetics in Mexicans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mexican population is highly diverse and has been shaped by different ancestral populations.
the Mexican population is a complex admixture of Amerindian and European ancestry, and to a lesser extent, African ancestry.
the HLA diversity is high and complex in Mexican admixed population, and the most common HLA haplotypes are from Amerindian origin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a high degree of diversity in HLA class I (HL-A) and class II (DRB1/DQB1) alleles and conserved extended Haplotypes (CEHS) in Mexicans.
the HLA blocks and HLA CEHs in Mexican admixed population are primarily of Amerindian and European origin.

HLA diversity and ancestral contribution in Mexican individuals is highly variable, and that the HLA blocks and HLA CEHs are mostly from Amerindian origin, with a small contribution of Caucasian, African and Asian ancestry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Mexican MHC is a complex admixture of Amerindian, European, and African ancestry.

we have described the HLA diversity and structure of Mexican individuals, which will be useful for genetic studies and for future research in the field of transplantation, immune responses and diseases.
